instructions.content: Treat the CloudWatch console as a micro-frontend SPA inside iframe[name="microConsole-Logs"]: window.document is the outer shell, so target the iframe contentDocument via page.frame({ name: 'microConsole-Logs' })
locator.click() on iframe elements times out after 5 s; use page.mouse.click(x, y) with coordinates built from the iframe bounding box plus the element's bounding box
The results table is its own scroll container (DIV.logs-table__wrapper); scroll it directly with frame.evaluate and scrollTop, not the window
Do not use this skill for services that do not use the microConsole iframe (for example S3 or EC2), where locator.click() works normally
If only a CloudWatch URL is needed without opening a browser, use aws-cloudwatch-url-builder instead
To reach Logs Insights: Services, CloudWatch, Logs, Logs Insights; select the log group, paste the query, set an Absolute time range, click Run query
For alarms: CloudWatch, Alarms, All alarms, search by name, click the alarm, and verify which metric is graphed before capturing screenshots
For metrics: CloudWatch, Metrics, All metrics, select the namespace, filter by dimension, Graph metrics, then adjust the time range in the graph toolbar
Get the frame reference first with page.frame({ name: 'microConsole-Logs' }), optionally caching it for reuse across operations
NEVER use locator.click() directly on CloudWatch iframe elements
NEVER use window.scrollBy() or window.scrollTo() inside the CloudWatch iframe
NEVER query window.document from page.evaluate() to interact with CloudWatch content; use frame.evaluate()
NEVER assume AWS/Lambda Errors = 0 means no alarm triggered: a Logs metric filter alarm fires on ERROR-level log lines even when the invocation exits cleanly
ALWAYS screenshot the alarm detail page, not the raw AWS/Lambda Errors metric graph
After opening the console for the chosen role, dismiss the cookie banner and the new-experience banner before navigating further
Set the region from the console header selector and confirm the matching region code (for example region=eu-west-1) appears in the URL
